newsitem.title: FRANCE: France deficit may be 3.4-3.5 pct - govt source.
newsitem.headline: France deficit may be 3.4-3.5 pct - govt source.

text.p: Early signs indicate France's 1997 public deficit to gross domestic product will be slightly above 3.4 to 3.5 percent, a government source said on Friday.
"What we know already is that there was slippage in the early part of the year, which puts us a little bit beyond 3.4 to 3.5 percent. But these are only first indications," the source said.
This would mean France would overshoot the Maastricht Treaty target for qualifying for monetary union which limits public deficits to three percent of GDP for 1997.

"We have to be very careful with estimates at this stage of the year," the source said, adding that France would do everything in its power to respect the commitment to launch monetary union on time on January 1, 1999.
The source said the decision to be taken next year by the European Union on which countries can join the single currency would be taken "on the basis of 1997 and the trend of 1998".

New French Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin, who campaigned against imposing further austerity to qualify for monetary union, has said the country's finances are in a serious state and has ordered an independent audit which is to report its findings on July 21.
